analysis.title: Softer US core CPI, finally?
key_insights: CACIB expects October US core CPI at 0.26% MoM SA, 2bp above the 0.24% Bloomberg average consensus and softer than 0.33% in September. August was 0.29%, boosted by noise in telephone services.

CACIB expects October US headline CPI at 0.29% MoM SA. No YoY figure can be calculated because the BLS never published the October 2025 index after last year's government shutdown, so there is no YoY consensus either.
The 3M moving average of core CPI, annualised, would come out at 3.53% in October on CACIB's forecast, the highest since January 2025.
With Brent crude down sharply, CACIB's model puts headline CPI at about 3.5-3.6% YoY until February 2027. The peak was 4.25% YoY in May 2026.

CACIB sees very limited second-round effects from higher energy prices tied to the Iran war, apart from airfares (1.3% of the core CPI basket). Some pass-through is appearing in core goods, but nothing significant yet.

Base effects will dominate core YoY. Last year's tariffs are rolling out of the YoY calculation, which lowers core goods CPI YoY. OER and rent YoY will be abnormally strong from November 2026 to March 2027 because of BLS methodology choices after the 2025 shutdown.
CACIB has core CPI around 2.5% YoY at an end-2027 horizon.

CACIB expects another 25bp Fed hike in December and a final 25bp hike in March. That would total 75bp of hikes, reversing last year's insurance cuts at an every-other-meeting pace, before another pause.
CACIB does not expect a major CPI impact from the blue wave result of the midterm election, beyond the lower crude prices already in its model.
Last Friday's payrolls report came in at +165k against a consensus of +70k, shifting focus to the inflation side of the Fed's mandate.

macro_indicators.interpretation: CACIB's forecast is 2bp above the 0.24% Bloomberg consensus and softer than September's 0.33%, but still firmer than ideal for the Fed.

risk_factors: Core CPI could come in firmer than CACIB's 0.26% forecast, as in August (0.29%) and September (0.33%).
Pass-through from higher energy prices into core goods could build beyond what is seen so far.
OER and rent YoY will be abnormally strong from November 2026 to March 2027 because of BLS methodology after the 2025 shutdown, which complicates the YoY reading.
geopolitical: Higher energy prices from the Iran war have produced very limited second-round effects in core CPI, apart from airfares.
The blue wave result of the midterm election is not expected to have a major CPI impact.
